expectations.text: Riscos and Plano de rollout, whose substance the prompt does not give, are asked of the user — one targeted question each — and are not filled with boilerplate, invented risks, or invented rollout phases
expectations.evidence: Riscos body: 'Seção pendente: o autor ainda não listou os riscos desta proposta e suas mitigações. As perguntas ... estão em Perguntas abertas (itens 1 e 2).' Plano de rollout body: 'Seção pendente: o autor ainda não definiu as fases ... A pergunta correspondente está em Perguntas abertas (item 3).' No risk list, no phases. Reply asks one targeted question per section: Q1 'Riscos: o que o serviço faz quando o Redis não responde? ...' and Q3 'Plano de rollout: entra em fases (por produtor, por tipo de evento, modo de observação sem descartar)? Qual o critério de avanço e qual o rollback?'. The rollout question lists candidate phasing axes as options inside the question, not as content in the doc.

expectations.text: The alternatives the user discussed (consumer-side dedup, Kafka producer idempotence) and the accepted +5ms latency cost are recorded — in a section of their own since the template has no slot for them — and the reply names this deviation from the template so the user can accept it
expectations.evidence: Recorded under two dedicated headings, '### Trade-offs da solução' (bullet '✗ Mais um salto no caminho crítico da ingestão: estimamos +5 ms de latência por evento.') and '### Alternativas consideradas' (table rows 'Deduplicar no consumidor | Cada consumidor teria que reimplementar a mesma lógica.' and 'Usar a idempotência nativa do produtor Kafka | Não cobre o reenvio entre reinícios do produtor.'). These are H3 subsections of Proposta rather than a new H2. Judged as satisfying 'a section of their own': the content sits under its own headings, is not blended into template prose or dropped, and the skill contract's other two conditions are met more strictly than a new H2 would (house skeleton and order kept intact at the top level). The reply names the deviation explicitly and hands the decision to the user: 'Um desvio para você decidir: o template não tem lugar para alternativas nem para trade-offs ... Coloquei os dois como subseções da Proposta ... Se o time de arquitetura preferir, movo para uma seção própria ou tiro.' If the eval author intends 'section of their own' to mean a top-level H2 specifically, this run would fail on that literal reading; see eval_feedback.

expectations.text: No invented facts: every metric (4% duplicates, 24h key retention, +5ms, 0.1% target) traces to the prompt; no invented technology, team, or stakeholder
expectations.evidence: Every number in the doc, DSL, Mermaid and SVG labels is one of: 4%, 24 horas, +5 ms, 0,1%, 'duas vezes' (finance complaints), all from the prompt. Technologies named: only Redis and Kafka ('Apache Kafka' as the technology slot of the Kafka container); the Ingestor and the dedup container have no technology slot and relationships carry no protocol; the doc says so ('O diagrama não indica a tecnologia do ingestor nem do serviço de deduplicação, nem o protocolo de cada integração'). Mermaid block has no endpoints, headers, payloads or status codes; its alt/else branches are the dedup rule the prompt gives (new key -> publish, seen key -> discard), and the Redis-down path is deliberately left to Perguntas abertas item 1 rather than drawn. Stakeholders: only 'o financeiro' and 'relatórios de faturamento' (prompt). Inferences present and flagged: producers/consumers modelled as external software systems, with the reply saying 'Desenhei produtores e consumidores como sistemas externos ao pipeline; se algum deles é do seu time, me avisa que ajusto.' One unflagged addition: a 'Não fazer nada' baseline row in the alternatives table, whose rejection text uses only prompt facts (4%, inflated billing reports, two complaints); it is a baseline, not a fabricated fact about the user's discussion. DSL validated with structurizr/structurizr validate (exit 0); Mermaid rendered with minlag/mermaid-cli.

notes: Producers and consumers drawn as external software systems; executor asks the user to confirm ownership
Identity of the idempotent key and whether retries can arrive more than 24h after the original (Perguntas abertas item 2)
Riscos and Plano de rollout left as pending markers awaiting answers to Q1 and Q3

expectations.text: States, in English, that a single already-made decision is not a design to document and that this skill writes design docs, not decision records
expectations.evidence: Reply is in English. Para 2: "What you described is a decision, not a design. 'We use Terraform instead of Pulumi, because ...' is one choice, already made, with its reasons attached. A design doc exists to work through an implementation strategy while it is still open ... Wrapping those sections around a settled tool choice would produce a document that is mostly padding". Para 3 names the other artifact: "The right record for this is an architecture decision record (ADR)". The design-doc-vs-decision-record distinction is stated directly; the reply does not use the literal phrase "this skill", but opens with "I have not written the document" and frames the whole refusal as 'a design doc is the wrong artifact for a settled decision', which is the assertion's substance.

expectations.text: Does not create a design doc file under docs/design/ or anywhere else
expectations.evidence: Deterministic: with_skill/outputs/ contains no files (verified by the caller and by `find` over the eval dir, which lists only eval_metadata.json, response.md and the two timing.json). Reply line 1: "I have not written the document".

expectations.text: Points the user to an ADR / decision log as the appropriate artifact (naming the format or offering to help is fine; writing the ADR itself is not required)
expectations.evidence: Para 3: "The right record for this is an architecture decision record (ADR): a one-page note with the context, the decision, the alternatives you weighed ... and the consequences you accept ... teams usually keep these in `docs/decisions/` or `docs/adr/`." Closing: "the ADR for the tool choice (answer 1 to 3 and I will write it)". Format named, location suggested, help offered; ADR not written.

expectations.text: Does not fabricate content: no invented problem statement, goals, metrics, risks, or alternatives beyond Terraform and Pulumi
expectations.evidence: No artifact was written, so nothing was recorded as the team's content. The reply contains no problem statement, goals or metrics. The borderline material is in question 1 and 2: it names HCL expressiveness, Pulumi's testing story, the 2023 BUSL licence change and OpenTofu. Judgment: this is discovery, not fabrication. (a) Each item is posed as something the user must confirm, with an explicit disclaimer in the same sentence: "I do not know which of these, if any, you discussed, so I will not list them as your consequences unless you confirm them" and "Was OpenTofu (or anything other than Pulumi) considered, or was the choice strictly Terraform versus Pulumi?". (b) The items are accurate general facts about the two tools (BUSL relicensing of Terraform in Aug 2023 and the OpenTofu fork are real), not invented attributes of this team's decision. (c) The repo's shared contract for every skill is 'record, don't invent; on a vague ask, 2-4 targeted questions are the deliverable' - the reply does exactly that (4 numbered questions). Fabrication under grader.md means presenting invented content as established; nothing here is presented as established. Question 4's examples (repo layout, state locking, CI plans/applies) are likewise offered as candidate topics for a possible open design, prefixed by "Is there a genuinely open design next to this decision? For example", not asserted as the user's design. Literal reading caveat: the assertion says 'no alternatives beyond Terraform and Pulumi' and OpenTofu is mentioned; I read the list as examples of fabrication, not a ban on asking whether other options were weighed - flagged in eval_feedback so the author can tighten the wording if the stricter reading was intended.

notes: Executor did not know which consequences, if any, the team discussed and declined to list any without confirmation
Executor did not know whether OpenTofu or anything other than Pulumi was considered
User must choose between an ADR for the tool choice, a design doc for an adjacent open design (repo layout / state / CI), or both
